references.text: The water in the Red Sea was divided when Moses stretched out his hand, just as the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant.
The command to keep Passover as a memorial for future generations, corresponding to stones as an everlasting memorial for the children of Israel.
Signs and reminders of the Lord's mighty deeds, like the stones that were to be a memorial forever.
The description of how the waters of Jordan were cut off when the priests with the ark of the covenant stood in the river.
The continuation of the explanation about the memorial stones and their purpose for future generations.
The command to tell the Lord's deeds to coming generations, just as the stones were to remind the children of Israel of the miracle at Jordan.
A poetic description of Jordan turning back, a reference to the same miracle at the crossing.
The exhortation to tell the children about God's mighty deeds when they ask, parallel to the explanation about the memorial stones.
